subject: Pinecrest - Deployment Segregation & Threat Surface Checklist
messages:
From: Erin O'Neil <erin.oneil@pinecrest-ins.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@pinecrest-ins.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment segregation and threat surface details request

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our procurement checklist we need a concise packet covering Redwood's deployment isolation and network controls so our security architecture team can complete the RFP. Could you please provide the following: 

- A high-level network diagram showing tenant isolation (control plane vs data plane), edge ingress pathways, and any sidecar/proxy placements.
- Short threat-surface summary (1 page) describing attacker paths you consider highest risk for multi-tenant inference (eg. cross-tenant leakage, KV cache exposure, control-plane compromise) and quick mitigations.
- Evidence pointers: SOC 2 coverage areas, audit log retention, KMS/HSM usage for customer keys, and where network-level logs are retained.
- Any restrictions or known limitations (eg. Egress restrictions, supported VPC peering topologies).

Delivery target: would appreciate a first-pass packet by EOD Thursday (2026-09-16). Also please include the right contact if we need follow-up technical interviews.

Regards,
Erin O'Neil
Senior Security Architect
Pinecrest Insurance

---
Attachment: pinecrest_request_template.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Erin O'Neil <erin.oneil@pinecrest-ins.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@pinecrest-ins.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment segregation and threat surface details request

Hi Erin,

Thanks — we can do that. I'll assemble a short packet that includes: a high-level network diagram, a one-page threat-surface summary, and a short table of evidence links (SOC 2, logging, KMS). Draft target: 2026-09-16 EOD as requested.

Proposed next step: a 30-minute technical review on Friday 2026-09-17 so we can walk the diagram and answer clarifying questions. Are you available 10:00–11:00 AM PT? If that works I will share a Zoom link and invite the engineering owners.

Contacts for follow-ups: Vanessa Ortiz (network & deployment diagrams), Rishi Malhotra (threat model / mitigations), Priyom Das (compliance / evidence). I'll loop them in.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Subject: Fwd: Pinecrest RFP - diagram + threat summary (draft request)
Team,

Forwarding Pinecrest's ask. They want a compact packet by EOD Thu (2026-09-16). Can we split deliverables as below and ship a consolidated PDF?

- Vanessa: high-level network diagram (control/data plane separation, tenant routing, sidecars, egress paths). One page + 1 appendix page listing IP flow examples.
- Rishi: 1-page threat-surface summary highlighting top 3 attack paths, assumed attacker capabilities, and short mitigation table.
- Priyom: list of evidence links and any redaction guidance (we should avoid internal hostnames).
Please attach files to your replies and mark anything that requires legal/compliance redaction. I'll handle the cover note and share the combined packet with Erin & Samir.

Thanks,
Chloe

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pinecrest RFP - diagram + threat summary (draft request)
Chloe —

Attached is the first draft of the network diagram and a short appendix describing expected egress routes for Hosted vs Dedicated. High-level notes below:

- Control plane is multi-tenant but access-controlled; customer data (inference requests & KV caches) stays in per-tenant data-plane pools.
- Sidecar proxies are used only on Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted uses an edge ingress layer + per-tenant routing tables.
- KV cache is scoped per-request and scrubbed on eviction; we call out mitigations for cross-tenant inference leakage (encryption at rest, tenant-scoped keys, strict cache key derivation).
I left internal hostnames redacted and replaced with generic labels. Attachment: pinecrest_net_diagram_v1.pdf (attachment stub).
I'll add a simple flow table for egress (NAT, peering, allowed endpoints) if you want that in the appendix.
-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Network Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@pinecrest-ins.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment segregation and threat surface details request - packet received
Chloe,
Thanks — we received the packet and the diagram (pinecrest_net_diagram_v1.pdf). That looks good as a first pass. A couple of quick clarifications before the call: 

1) Can you confirm whether the KV cache encryption uses customer-managed keys (BYOK) in Private deployments, or only Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted?
2) For Dedicated deployments, do sidecars terminate TLS or is TLS terminated at the edge and proxied inside the VPC?
3) Could you share the HubSpot deal id or a pointer to the evidence manifest so our compliance team can reference the SOC 2 pages?
We're good to meet on 2026-09-17 10:30 AM PT — Erin, does that still work for you? We'll plan for a 30-minute technical run-through. Please attach the final packet (combined PDF) and a short evidence manifest CSV so our reviewers can track items.
Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Best,
Samir Gupta
Director, Infrastructure Security
Pinecrest Insurance
